title: Joint H1 injectivity of residue-field product slices
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$ be proper morphisms of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-scheme], with sections $\sigma:S\to X$ and $\tau:S\to Y$ [def-pc-section]. Suppose their canonical structure-pushforward units are isomorphisms after every base change [def-pc-base-change, lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. For $s\in S$ put $p:X\times_S Y\to S$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and let $i_X=(1,\tau f):X\to X\times_S Y$ and $i_Y=(\sigma g,1):Y\to X\times_S Y$. Then the base changes of these maps along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ induce an injective map $H^1((X\times_S Y)_s,\mathcal O)\to H^1(X_s,\mathcal O)\times H^1(Y_s,\mathcal O)$ [def-sc-structure-sheaf-cohomology-pullback, def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0BF3, first sentence of proof: Kunneth injectivity on the special fibre (Tag 0BED)

proof.text: Evaluate universal structure pushforward at Spec κ(s). Identify the canonical scalar maps with its maps on global sections to obtain H0(X_s,O)=κ(s) and H0(Y_s,O)=κ(s). Base change the sections to rational points. Properness is stable under base change. Apply picard_h1_product_injective over κ(s).

Pullback pasting identifies the chosen residue fibre of X×_S Y with X_s×_κ(s)Y_s and identifies its base-changed section maps with the two rational-point slices. Functoriality of structure-sheaf cohomology transports the preceding injectivity along this isomorphism.
